participants: Andrew Musial (closer; recorded under the Fathom speaker label 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)')
summary: Full team meeting with the longest coaching block in this batch. Wins and pipeline first: the team is pacing 20 units and $80K, Andrew needs $3,800 more to hit $50K, Richard needs roughly $9,000, Kim needs six more sets, and everyone is opening Sunday slots. Andrew reports a live prospect with diabetes who has a competing appointment with a diabetes-specialist trainer, and the manager coaches him on how to argue past that specialist. The second half is a recorded call review of one of Richard's objection-handling calls, covering how to answer 'is it a one-time fee', why commitment must be secured in discovery rather than after the price drop, and at length why a rep who leans in emotionally kills the sale — the manager's 'oak tree energy' and neutrality framework, plus tactical work on using silence after the price. It closes with pipeline admin and a request for Skool community moderator access. The recording cuts off mid-sentence during a follow-on 1-1 between Chris and Richard.
notable: The most consequential exchange in the batch: a manager giving clinical direction about a diabetic prospect and coaching the closer to argue past a diabetes-specialist trainer the prospect has already booked — 'as long as their insulin is in check and they're going to the doctor for that, then they need to be moving more or they need to just watch the amount of insulin... which is exactly what the primal nutrition plan will do for them' and 'he just needs to move more and eat less.'
The same prospect's eating was described by the closer as stress-driven compulsive eating; the manager's response was 'You just gotta feel the urge underneath it and not eat.'

Stated internal definition of a lost deal: 'That's never lost until they tell you straight up no.' Any close-rate the company reports will therefore differ from an audit that resolves dispositions per call.

A prospect who paid a deposit has gone quiet and is being chased rather than refunded: 'the guy that did the deposit, kind of continue following up with him. He is, like, barely responding to me, but I think that he just maybe got a little bit fearful.'

Scripted deflection when a prospect asks about payment structure: 'Most people take care of it up front and throw it on a credit card. Why do you ask?' — the manager's stated reason is 'Because it puts it back on them.' The team also flagged that saying 'usually it's a one-time fee' invites a worse question.

The closer described urinating into a bottle under his desk mid-call while taking a payment on a previous offer, because 'that guy was very on the fence, so I didn't want to give him any space.' The manager corrected it firmly: 'Andrew, don't do that here.' Consistent with the never-give-space norm set out in the 06/22 meeting.

Two live prospects are being correctly held pending medical results — an anesthesiologist who has gone silent and a fit 59-year-old who 'cannot commit before he has his results back' — which is the right handling and worth recording alongside the diabetes exchange.
The closer disclosed his own diagnosed genetic hip degeneration: 'your hips look like you're in like an 80 year old.'

Business context: projections for next month will be roughly half, an additional overflow closer is joining, and one closer is still working a second sales offer concurrently — 'I'm probably going to leave the other offer anyway.'
Primal University at $2K for a year is still under discussion with Trevor and not yet approved: 'We're not moving on it yet, but it is interesting, and we're going to talk to Trevor about it.'
The recording ends mid-sentence at 01:01:55 during a private follow-on between the manager and Richard, so the end of the meeting is not captured.
